title: Barbarossa: the first hundred days (22 Jun - 30 Sep 1941)

briefing.historical: On 22 June 1941 more than 3.8 million Axis troops invaded the Soviet Union along a 2,900 km front. Army Group North drove through the Baltic states toward Leningrad, Army Group Centre took Brest, Minsk and Smolensk, and Army Group South destroyed Soviet armies at Uman and Kiev. Typhoon, the drive on Moscow, began on 30 September (R01).
briefing.situation: The Germans must destroy the frontier armies and take the key cities before the logistics, distance and weather wear the offensive down; the Soviets must trade space for time, hold the Dvina-Dnieper and Luga lines and keep Leningrad, Kiev and Moscow. Armies and panzer groups are the units; strengths are game-scale and every start position is approximate. Romanian and Finnish forces, the Southern Front, air and naval forces are not modelled (not retrieved).

playableNations.summary: Encircle the frontier armies and take Minsk, Smolensk, Kiev and the approaches to Leningrad.
Survive the surprise, trade space for time and hold Leningrad, Kiev and Moscow.

GAME-SCALE ABSTRACTION (internal): manpower, equipment, morale/experience, readiness/organisation, resources, objective points, thresholds, supply capacities, hub ramp times, air-supremacy radius and speed are nominal game values, not historical strengths. Sourced aggregates anchoring them: 153 German divisions (R01), Panzer Group 1 799 tanks (R12), Western Front 25+13+7 divisions (R04), Brest garrison about 9,000 and 45th ID about 17,000 (R10).
LOCATION POLICY (internal): locations are real cities/towns placed at Wikipedia (R17) coordinates, nudged to the nearest land cell of the terrain grid where needed.

POSITION POLICY (internal): no retrieved source gives army or corps start coordinates; unit positions are approximate sector anchors inferred from the named towns and areas in R01-R16, with a small deterministic spread. Every unit position is APPROXIMATE.
BORDER POLICY (internal): initialControl is a coarse 1941 demarcation line (German-held Poland and East Prussia west of it, Soviet-held ground east of it); no source gives exact lines.

RAIL-GAUGE POLICY (internal): the Soviet broad-gauge rail needing conversion is not in the retrieved text; Axis forward hubs (Brest, Minsk, Smolensk and others) are capture-activated supply sources with a game-scale throughput ramp (rampHours) standing in for gauge conversion. The engine has no gauge concept, so Soviet rail still counts as usable rail for the Axis (too generous; flagged in KNOWN_ISSUES).
